0028 Sti ﬀ-Limb Syndrome: Thinking about that!
Alicia Delorme 1, Daniela Elena Pencu 2, Gaetan de Saint-Hubert 1
1Internal Medecine Department, Grand hôpital de Charleroi, Gilly, Belgium; 2Internal Medecine Department, Grand Hôpital de Charleroi,

The acquired results pointed towards a diagnosis of systemic capillary leak syndrome.
Initially, treatment with a leukotrein antagonist (montelukast 10 mg), theophylline (xanthium
400 mg) and H1 antagonists (ranitidine 300 mg, ceterizine 10 mg) was started. Therapy didn ’t
work and the patient complained of total body pain and a limited range of movement. Based
on some published cases, treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins (Multigam 5 %) was
given. First time after administration there was an improvement with a weight loss up to 20
kilos. After three times, the e ﬀect was insu ﬃ cient. The patient was su ﬀering from increasing
edema and orthopnea. Because of the refractory character of the disease and the increasing
complaints, a combination therapy of Velcade (Bortezomide, a proteasome inhibitor) –
Cyclophosphamide (chemotherapeutic drug) – Dexamethason was started, which is normally
given in case of a multiple myeloma. After 5 cycli, IgG к was decreased from 6,31 g/l to 3,03 g/
l and the patient was no longer su ﬀering from acute episodes of edema. There was still some
peripheral edema, especially at the lower limbs. Due to the therapy, polyneuropathy of
ﬁngers and toes, extreme fatigue and full-blown diabetes (fasting glucose 795 mg/dl) arose.
Hyperglycemia caused a blurred vision. Next cyclus, therapy was changed into a lower dose
of dexamethasone and cyclophosphamide was removed, which reduced the symptoms.
Conclusion: This 52-year-old man su ﬀered from an idiopathic systemic capillary leak syn-
drome in presence of IgG к paraprotein. Conventional treatment options didn ’t work so a
combination therapy of Velcade-Cyclofosfamide-Dexamethasone, what is normally given for
multiple myeloma, was started. The therapy resulted in a partial remission of paraprotein IgG
к and acute events of edema disappeared. There was still edema at the lower extremities and
some side e ﬀects from VCD treatment.
ABSTRACT
Introduction:T h es t iﬀ-person syndrome (SPS) is a rare neurological disorder characterized by
muscle stiﬀness and recurrent episodes of painful muscle spasms in the trunk and limbs. Several
subtypes exist such as the classic SPS that aﬀects all muscles and provokes truncal stiﬀness. Rarely
it can be a paraneoplastic syndrome . Another atypical form called Sti ﬀ-Limb Syndrome (Partial
SPS) and only a ﬀects the legs. The etiology is unclear but the presence of Anti-GAD antibodies
suggests an auto-immune origin. The antibodies inhibit GABAergic circuits inducting a neuronal
hyper-excitability. In it’s classic form, 30% of the patients are type I diabetics .
Case Report: A 52-year-old man of African descent is admitted to the emergency department
with the following symptoms: muscle cramps and continuous painful spasms in both legs for
the past 2 weeks, increased tiredness and restricted mobility. He has no medical history. His
general practitioner prescribed him magnesium but the condition has not improved. Clinical
examination showed continuous muscle spasms in both calves and quadriceps and involun-
tary thumb shaking . No sensory or motor de ﬁcit was observed but a Chvostek sign was
noted . The blood tests showed a high rate of creatine kinase and a monoclonal IgG Lambda
component. No ionic disorders were found with normal rates of calcium and magnesium
observed. Cerebral and cervical RMN showed a negligible narrowing of the cervical canal. The
cerebrospinal ﬂuid did not show any abnormality. Electromyography found fasciculations of
twin muscles. No electric signs of polyneuritis or myogenous defect were noted. The rate of
anti-GAD antibodies was increased . The patient was treated with Diazepam 5 mg four times a
day and after 5 days a decrease of the spasms was observed. Three weeks after the treatment
an electromyography and a blood test showed that the spasms had almost disappear and
that the level of creatine kinase in blood test was normal.
Conclusion: The diagnosis of Sti ﬀ-person syndrome is not based on an individual test but is
rather a hypothesis supported by the following criteria:
-Episodic spams
-A positive therapeutic response to oral diazepam (evaluated by electromyography)
-An absence of other neurologic disorders

anti-gephyrin may be present in GAD-negative patients. The lack of antibodies does not
exclude a SPS.
The prognosis for patients with sti ﬀ-person syndrome is guarded. A functional decline is
generally noted in most patients.
ABSTRACT
Objectives: The primary objective of this case report is to report a rare association between
two chronic in ﬂammatory diseases.
Background: The overlap syndrome between an autoimmune hepatitis and a systemic lupus
erythematosus is rare. The liver involvement in a systemic lupus erythematosus is variable. It
is mostly limited to alterations in the liver function tests (60%) and less frequently to a true
hepatitis. When it occurs, the liver biopsy seems to be essential to reach the diagnosis.
Case report : A 71-year-old woman, without speci ﬁc medical history, was admitted in our
department of internal medicine for fatigue, lack of appetite and weight loss (3kg in 2 weeks)
and arthralgia.
Investigations revealed anaemia and neutropenia, elevated acute phase reactants, cytolysis,
cholestasis and renal insu ﬃ ciency. After having excluded malignancy, infection, viral hepatitis,
toxics (AINS) and alcohol, a liver biopsy and positive autoimmune serology (ANA and anti-Sm
antibodies) enabled us to reach the diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis associated with a
systemic lupus erythematosus.
Conclusion: We reported a case of a 71-year-old woman with an overlap syndrome between
an autoimmune hepatitis and a systemic lupus erythematosus, a rare association. It is crucial
to make the di ﬀerence between the overlap syndrome and the lupus hepatitis since the latter
is extremely rare in the beginning of a lupus. Therefore, the liver biopsy is essential for the
diagnosis.
ABSTRACT

cidence on imaging techniques (2).
